objects.description: Doubly linked list node used as an intrusive list hook. Each container embeds a struct list_head member and links nodes via next/prev pointers. The list head is a sentinel whose next/prev initially point to itself.
Represents a source/location record used by the Kconfig system, with linkage to a sibling list (next), a hierarchical parent, file name, and a current line number.
Three-valued logic used by Kconfig to represent disabled (no), module (mod), and enabled (yes) states.
Operation/type tags for expression nodes in Kconfig condition trees.
Variant payload used in expression nodes, holding either a subexpression pointer or a symbol pointer.
Binary/unary expression node for Kconfig logic. The type field declares the operator or atom kind, and left/right carry subexpressions or symbols depending on type.
Pairs a dependency expression with its evaluated tristate value.
Holds a symbol’s concrete value (string/number/choice via val) along with its tristate for boolean/tristate symbols.
Classification of Kconfig symbols by value domain.
Represents a Kconfig symbol, including its name, type, current and default values, visibility, flags, properties, and dependency expressions (direct, reverse, and implied).

objects.definition:
enum prop_type {
	P_UNKNOWN,
	P_PROMPT,	/* prompt "foo prompt" or "BAZ Value" */
	P_COMMENT,	/* text associated with a comment */
	P_MENU,	    /* prompt associated with a menu or menuconfig symbol */
	P_DEFAULT,	/* default y */
	P_CHOICE,	/* choice value */
	P_SELECT,	/* select BAR */
	P_IMPLY,	/* imply BAR */
	P_RANGE,	/* range 7..100 (for a symbol) */
	P_SYMBOL,	/* where a symbol is defined */
	P_RESET,	/* reset to defaults condition */
};
objects.description: Kinds of properties that may be attached to Kconfig symbols and menu nodes.
A node describing a single property of a symbol or menu entry, such as prompts, defaults, selects, and ranges, including its condition, visibility, and source location.

Represents a node in the Kconfig menu tree, linking hierarchical structure, the associated symbol (if any), prompts, visibility/depends expressions, help text, file location, and frontend-specific data.
Entry used for jump-to functionality in UIs, linking into a list, with an offset/key and a target menu node.
Growable string buffer utility with length, dynamic char buffer, and optional wrapping width hint.

functions.name: list_empty
functions.signature: static inline int list_empty(const struct list_head *head)
functions.description: Tests whether a doubly-linked Linux-kernel-style list is empty by checking if head->next points back to head. Typical usage: to guard iteration or removal on a possibly-empty list head initialized with LIST_HEAD or LIST_HEAD_INIT.
requirements: head must be a valid, initialized list_head acting as a list head (e.g., created with LIST_HEAD or LIST_HEAD_INIT).
head must be non-NULL.

functions.name: list_add_tail
functions.signature: static inline void list_add_tail(struct list_head *_new, struct list_head *head)
functions.description: Adds a new entry at the tail (before the head) of a doubly-linked Linux-kernel-style list. Useful for implementing FIFO queues.
requirements: head must be a valid, initialized list head of a circular doubly-linked list.
_new must be a valid list node whose next/prev are not currently linked into another list (callers typically ensure the node is not already in a list).
Both pointers must be non-NULL.

functions.name: list_del
functions.description: Removes an entry from a doubly-linked Linux-kernel-style list and poisons its next/prev pointers. After deletion, the entry is in an undefined state and must not be reused without reinitialization.
requirements: entry must be a valid node currently linked into a list.
entry must be non-NULL.
Do not use the entry’s next/prev after deletion unless reinitialized; list_empty() on the entry itself is not meaningful post-deletion.

functions.name: lookup_file
functions.description: Looks up and returns a file record by name within the internal file tracking used by the Kconfig system. Returns a pointer to an existing struct file or possibly NULL if not found (exact behavior not documented here).
requirements: name should be a valid, null-terminated string pointer.
Behavior on unknown name is not specified in this header; callers should be prepared for a NULL return.

functions.name: expr_alloc_symbol
functions.description: Allocates and returns an expression node representing the given symbol.
requirements: sym should be a valid pointer to a struct symbol.
Return may be NULL on allocation failure (not documented).

functions.name: expr_alloc_one
functions.signature: struct expr *expr_alloc_one(enum expr_type type, struct expr *ce)
functions.description: Allocates an expression node of the given type with a single child/operand.
requirements: type must be a valid expr_type that accepts a single child (e.g., E_NOT, E_SYMBOL, etc.; exact mapping not specified).
ce may be NULL depending on type; behavior not specified.
Return may be NULL on allocation failure (not documented).

functions.name: expr_alloc_two
functions.signature: struct expr *expr_alloc_two(enum expr_type type, struct expr *e1, struct expr *e2)
functions.description: Allocates an expression node of the given type with two children/operands, such as logical or comparison expressions.
requirements: type must be a valid binary expr_type (e.g., E_AND, E_OR, comparisons; exact mapping not specified).
e1 and e2 may be NULL depending on context; behavior not specified.
Return may be NULL on allocation failure (not documented).

functions.name: expr_alloc_comp
functions.signature: struct expr *expr_alloc_comp(enum expr_type type, struct symbol *s1, struct symbol *s2)
functions.description: Allocates a comparison expression node of the given type between two symbols (e.g., E_EQUAL, E_UNEQUAL, range comparisons).
requirements: type should be a comparison expr_type (E_EQUAL, E_UNEQUAL, E_LTH, E_LEQ, E_GTH, E_GEQ).
s1 and s2 should be valid pointers to struct symbol.
Return may be NULL on allocation failure (not documented).

functions.name: expr_alloc_and
functions.description: Convenience allocation for a logical AND expression with two child expressions.
requirements: e1 and e2 should be valid (non-NULL) expr pointers; NULL handling is not documented.
Return may be NULL on allocation failure (not documented).

functions.name: expr_alloc_or
functions.description: Convenience allocation for a logical OR expression with two child expressions.
requirements: e1 and e2 should be valid (non-NULL) expr pointers; NULL handling is not documented.
Return may be NULL on allocation failure (not documented).

functions.name: expr_copy
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of the given expression tree.
requirements: org should be a valid pointer to an expression; behavior for NULL is not specified.
Return may be NULL on allocation failure (not documented).

functions.name: expr_free
functions.description: Frees an expression node or tree previously allocated by expr_alloc_* or expr_copy.
requirements: e may be NULL or non-NULL; exact NULL handling not specified.
e must not be used after this call.

functions.name: expr_eliminate_eq
functions.description: Simplifies or eliminates equality-related structures within two expressions, possibly modifying the expressions in place through the provided pointers. Exact transformation details are not documented here.
requirements: ep1 and ep2 must be non-NULL pointers to expr* locations that may be updated.
The expressions referenced by *ep1 and *ep2 should be valid or NULL.

functions.name: expr_eq
functions.description: Compares two expressions for structural or semantic equality and returns nonzero if equal, zero otherwise.
requirements: e1 and e2 may be NULL; exact semantics for NULL are not specified.
Return value is an int used as a boolean.

functions.name: expr_calc_value
functions.description: Evaluates the given expression and returns its tristate value (n, m, y).
requirements: e may be NULL; semantics for NULL not specified here.
Caller should handle all possible tristate return values.

functions.name: expr_trans_bool
functions.description: Transforms an expression to an equivalent or simplified boolean form. Exact rules are not documented here.
requirements: e may be NULL or non-NULL; behavior for NULL not specified.
Returned expression must be freed by caller with expr_free when no longer needed (inferred from allocation pattern).

functions.name: expr_eliminate_dups
functions.description: Eliminates duplicate subexpressions from the expression tree and returns the simplified expression. Exact strategy is not documented here.
requirements: e should be a valid expression or NULL; behavior not specified for NULL.
Returned expression ownership likely transfers to caller; free when done (inferred).

functions.name: expr_transform
functions.description: Applies general transformations to an expression tree, potentially simplifying or normalizing it. Specific transformations are not documented here.
requirements: e should be a valid expression or NULL; behavior not specified for NULL.
Returned expression should be managed by caller and freed when done (inferred).

functions.name: expr_contains_symbol
functions.description: Checks whether the expression tree contains a reference to the specified symbol. Returns nonzero if found, zero otherwise.
requirements: dep may be NULL or non-NULL; behavior for NULL not documented.
sym should be a valid symbol pointer.

functions.name: expr_depends_symbol
functions.description: Determines whether the expression depends on the given symbol (i.e., if the symbol affects the value of the expression).
requirements: dep may be NULL or non-NULL; exact NULL semantics not documented.
sym should be a valid symbol pointer.

functions.name: expr_trans_compare
functions.signature: struct expr *expr_trans_compare(struct expr *e, enum expr_type type, struct symbol *sym)
functions.description: Transforms or reduces a comparison-related expression against a symbol, based on the specified comparison type. Exact behavior is not documented here.
requirements: e should be a valid expression pointer.
type should be an appropriate comparison expr_type.
sym should be a valid symbol pointer.
Returned expression should be freed by caller when no longer needed (inferred).

functions.name: expr_fprint
functions.description: Prints a textual representation of the expression to the given FILE stream.
requirements: out must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.
e may be NULL or non-NULL; exact output for NULL not documented.

functions.name: expr_gstr_print
functions.description: Appends a textual representation of the expression to the given growable string buffer (gstr).
requirements: gs must be a valid pointer to a struct gstr previously initialized with str_new (or otherwise valid).
e may be NULL; exact output for NULL not documented.

functions.name: expr_gstr_print_revdep
functions.signature: void expr_gstr_print_revdep(struct expr *e, struct gstr *gs, tristate pr_type, const char *title)
functions.description: Appends a textual representation of reverse dependencies for the expression into the growable string, optionally filtered or formatted by pr_type and title. Exact formatting is not documented here.
requirements: gs must be a valid gstr.
title may be NULL or non-NULL; behavior not documented.
pr_type must be a valid tristate value.

functions.name: zconfdump
functions.description: Dumps configuration-related information to the provided FILE stream. Exact content and format are not documented here.
requirements: out must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.

functions.name: zconf_starthelp
functions.description: Begins a help-text collection/processing mode for the Kconfig parser. Exact behavior is not documented here.
requirements: No arguments; may affect global parser state; should be called within appropriate parsing context (inferred from name).

functions.name: zconf_fopen
functions.description: Opens a configuration-related file by name and returns a FILE* stream reference. Wrapper around fopen with Kconfig-specific search paths or logic (inferred).
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated file path string.
Caller is responsible for closing the returned FILE* with fclose when done.

functions.name: zconf_initscan
functions.description: Initializes the lexical scanner for the given file or source. Sets up scanner state for subsequent calls to yylex (inferred).
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated string identifying a file to scan.
Must be called before scanning tokens from that source.

functions.name: zconf_nextfile
functions.description: Switches the scanner to the next file/source in an include-like mechanism. Exact behavior is not documented here.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated string path.
Should be used after initializing scanning; impacts global scanner state.

functions.name: zconf_lineno
functions.description: Returns the current input line number from the scanner/parser.
requirements: None beyond initialized scanner state (inferred).

functions.name: zconf_curname
functions.description: Returns the current input file name being processed by the scanner/parser.
requirements: None beyond initialized scanner state (inferred).
Returned pointer is owned by the system and must not be freed by the caller (inferred).

functions.name: conf_get_configname
functions.description: Returns the path or name of the primary configuration file (e.g., .config).
requirements: Returned pointer is managed by the configuration system and should not be freed (inferred).

functions.name: set_all_choice_values
functions.description: Sets default or resolved choice values for the given choice symbol across its alternatives. Exact policy not documented here.
requirements: csym must be a valid pointer to a symbol that represents a choice (sym_is_choice(csym) likely true).

functions.name: file_lookup
functions.description: Looks up and possibly creates/returns a file struct for the given name within internal tracking (distinct from lookup_file; exact semantics not documented).
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Caller should handle a NULL return gracefully if not found (behavior not documented).

functions.name: xmalloc
functions.description: Allocates size bytes of memory, like malloc, but with Kconfig-specific error handling (often aborts on failure; not documented here).
requirements: size specifies the number of bytes to allocate; 0-size behavior is per implementation (not documented).
Returned pointer should be freed with free when no longer needed.

functions.name: xcalloc
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized memory for an array, like calloc, with Kconfig-specific error handling (not documented here).
requirements: nmemb and size specify the array dimensions; beware of overflow (behavior not documented).
Returned pointer should be freed with free when no longer needed.

functions.name: xrealloc
functions.description: Resizes a previously allocated memory block, like realloc, with Kconfig-specific error handling (not documented here).
requirements: p may be NULL to allocate new memory.
size specifies the new size in bytes; 0-size behavior is implementation-defined (not documented).
Returned pointer should be freed with free when no longer needed.

functions.name: xstrdup
functions.description: Duplicates a string, like strdup, with Kconfig-specific error handling (not documented here).
requirements: s must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Returned string must be freed with free.

functions.name: xstrndup
functions.description: Duplicates at most n bytes of a string, ensuring NUL-termination, like strndup, with Kconfig-specific error handling (not documented here).
requirements: s must be a valid pointer; treated as a C string up to n characters.
Returned string must be freed with free.

functions.name: yylex
functions.description: Lexical scanner function that returns the next token for the Kconfig parser.
requirements: Must be called after scanner has been initialized (e.g., via zconf_initscan).
Returns an int token code; 0 or EOF per lexer conventions when input ends (not documented).

functions.name: str_new
functions.description: Creates and returns a new growable string buffer (gstr) initialized to an empty state.
requirements: No arguments. The returned struct gstr should be passed to str_free when done to release internal resources.

functions.name: str_free
functions.description: Frees resources associated with a growable string buffer created by str_new.
requirements: gs must be a valid pointer to a gstr previously obtained from str_new or equivalent initialization.
Do not use the gstr after freeing.

functions.name: str_append
functions.description: Appends a C string to the growable string buffer.
requirements: gs must be a valid pointer to an initialized gstr.
s should be a valid, null-terminated string; behavior for NULL is not documented.

functions.name: str_printf
functions.description: Appends formatted text to the growable string buffer, printf-style.
requirements: gs must be a valid pointer to an initialized gstr.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; additional arguments must match format specifiers.

functions.name: str_get
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal C string contained in the growable string buffer, suitable for reading. Ownership and lifetime are managed by the gstr.
requirements: gs must be a valid pointer to an initialized gstr.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller; becomes invalid after str_free or further modifications (inferred).

functions.name: _menu_init
functions.description: Initializes global menu structures for the Kconfig system.
requirements: Must be called before other menu manipulation functions (inferred).

functions.name: menu_warn
functions.description: Emits a formatted warning related to a specific menu node.
requirements: menu may be NULL or non-NULL; exact handling not documented.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; additional arguments must match.

functions.name: menu_add_menu
functions.description: Begins a new submenu/menu context and returns the created menu node.
requirements: Must be used within proper menu construction sequencing; relies on global menu state (inferred).
Caller receives a menu* managed by the menu system; ownership semantics not documented.

functions.name: menu_end_menu
functions.description: Ends the current submenu/menu context.
requirements: There must be a current open menu context to end; relies on prior calls to menu_add_menu (inferred).

functions.name: menu_add_entry
functions.description: Adds a menu entry for the given symbol to the current menu context.
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a symbol.
Requires an initialized/current menu context (inferred).

functions.name: menu_add_dep
functions.description: Adds a dependency expression to the current menu context.
requirements: dep should be a valid expression pointer; NULL handling not documented.
Requires an initialized/current menu context (inferred).

functions.name: menu_add_visibility
functions.description: Adds a 'visible if' dependency to the current menu node; multiple visibility dependencies are ANDed (per struct menu doc).
requirements: dep should be a valid expression pointer; NULL handling not documented.
Requires a current menu node/context (inferred).

functions.name: menu_add_prop
functions.signature: struct property *menu_add_prop(enum prop_type type, struct expr *expr, struct expr *dep)
functions.description: Adds a property of the specified type to the current symbol/menu node, with an optional conditional expression and dependency.
requirements: type must be a valid prop_type.
expr and dep may be NULL per property type semantics (not documented here).
Requires a current menu context (inferred).

functions.name: menu_add_prompt
functions.signature: struct property *menu_add_prompt(enum prop_type type, char *prompt, struct expr *dep)
functions.description: Adds a prompt or text (for symbol prompt, menu title, or comment) with an optional dependency to the current menu node.
requirements: type should be P_PROMPT, P_MENU, or P_COMMENT per usage (inferred).
prompt must be a valid null-terminated string pointer.
dep may be NULL.
Requires a current menu context (inferred).

functions.name: menu_add_expr
functions.signature: void menu_add_expr(enum prop_type type, struct expr *expr, struct expr *dep)
functions.description: Adds an expression-type property (e.g., default, select, imply, range) with an optional dependency to the current menu node.
requirements: type must be a valid prop_type for expression properties (e.g., P_DEFAULT, P_SELECT, P_IMPLY, P_RANGE).
expr should be a valid expression; dep may be NULL.
Requires a current menu context (inferred).

functions.name: menu_add_symbol
functions.signature: void menu_add_symbol(enum prop_type type, struct symbol *sym, struct expr *dep)
functions.description: Associates a symbol with the current menu node for a property of the specified type, optionally under a dependency.
requirements: type must be a valid prop_type that carries a symbol (e.g., P_CHOICE, P_SYMBOL; refer to comments).
sym must be a valid symbol pointer.
dep may be NULL.
Requires a current menu context (inferred).

functions.name: menu_finalize
functions.description: Finalizes the menu tree beneath the given parent, computing derived data such as visibility and dependencies. Exact details not documented.
requirements: parent must be a valid pointer to a menu node (or possibly NULL for root; not documented).

functions.name: menu_set_type
functions.description: Sets the type (e.g., S_BOOLEAN, S_TRISTATE, etc.) for the current symbol/menu context. The exact mapping from int to symbol types is not documented here.
requirements: Requires that a current symbol/menu context exists (inferred).
type must be a valid symbol type value (inferred).

functions.name: menu_is_empty
functions.description: Returns whether the given menu node has no visible/usable entries. Exact criteria are implementation-defined and not documented here.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.

functions.name: menu_is_visible
functions.description: Returns whether the given menu node is visible given its dependencies.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.

functions.name: menu_has_prompt
functions.description: Returns whether the menu node has an associated prompt/text property.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.

functions.name: menu_get_prompt
functions.description: Returns the prompt string associated with the menu node, if any.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.
Returned pointer is managed by the menu system and should not be freed by the caller (inferred).

functions.name: menu_get_parent_menu
functions.description: Returns the parent menu node for the given menu node.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.

functions.name: menu_has_help
functions.description: Returns whether the menu node has associated help text.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.

functions.name: menu_get_help
functions.description: Returns the help text associated with the menu node, if any.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.
Returned pointer is managed by the menu system and should not be freed by the caller (inferred).

functions.name: get_jump_key_char
functions.description: Returns an integer character code for a jump key used by front ends to navigate to configuration items. Exact mapping not documented here.
requirements: No arguments; depends on UI/frontend state (inferred).

functions.name: get_relations_str
functions.signature: struct gstr get_relations_str(struct symbol **sym_arr, struct list_head *head)
functions.description: Builds and returns a formatted growable string containing relation information for the given set of symbols and an auxiliary list (e.g., jump targets).
requirements: sym_arr must be a valid pointer to an array of symbol pointers; array termination/length is not documented.
head must be a valid list_head pointing to a list of jump_key entries (inferred from struct jump_key).
Returned gstr must be cleaned up with str_free when done.

functions.name: menu_get_ext_help
functions.description: Retrieves extended help for the given menu node and appends it into the provided growable string buffer.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.
help must be a valid pointer to an initialized gstr.

functions.name: sym_clear_all_valid
functions.description: Clears the SYMBOL_VALID flag on all symbols, forcing recalculation of their current values.
requirements: No arguments. Intended to be called before recomputation of symbol values.

functions.name: sym_choice_default
functions.description: Returns the default selected symbol within a choice, according to default rules and dependencies.
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a symbol that represents a choice.

functions.name: sym_get_range_prop
functions.description: Returns the range property (P_RANGE) associated with a numeric symbol, if any.
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a symbol.

functions.name: sym_get_string_default
functions.description: Returns the default string value for a string symbol, if defined.
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a symbol.
Returned pointer lifetime/ownership is not documented; treat as read-only.

functions.name: sym_check_deps
functions.description: Checks dependencies for the given symbol and returns a symbol pointer (possibly the same) indicating problematic or related information. Exact semantics are not documented here.
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a symbol.

functions.name: prop_get_symbol
functions.description: Returns the symbol associated with a property (if the property type carries a symbol).
requirements: prop must be a valid pointer to a property that references a symbol.

functions.name: sym_get_tristate_value
functions.description: Returns the current tristate value (n, m, y) for the specified symbol: sym->curr.tri.
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a struct symbol.

functions.name: sym_get_choice_value
functions.description: Returns the currently selected symbol within a choice from sym->curr.val, cast to struct symbol*.
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a struct symbol representing a choice.
Returned pointer may be NULL if no selection; not documented.

functions.name: sym_is_choice
functions.description: Returns true if the symbol has the SYMBOL_CHOICE flag set, indicating it represents a choice.
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a struct symbol.

functions.name: sym_is_choice_value
functions.description: Returns true if the symbol has the SYMBOL_CHOICEVAL flag set, indicating it is a member of a choice.
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a struct symbol.

functions.name: sym_is_optional
functions.description: Returns true if the symbol (usually a choice) is optional (SYMBOL_OPTIONAL flag).
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a struct symbol.

functions.name: sym_has_value
functions.description: Returns true if the symbol has a user-provided value (SYMBOL_DEF_USER flag set).
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a struct symbol.
